summary.text: Missi Hesketh, a Democrat and former alderwoman and mayor of Forsyth, Missouri, lost the November 3, 2026 election for Missouri's 7th District to Eric Burlison.
She worked in food service, clerical and finance jobs before a career in education.

paragraphs.text: Hesketh was born in Elmhurst, Illinois, in 1971, according to her Ballotpedia survey.
She moved to Forsyth, Missouri, with her family in 1983 and graduated from Forsyth High School in 1990.
She describes attending the University of Missouri for one semester before working in food service, clerical and finance jobs, and says a post-9/11 job change steered her toward education.

Hesketh earned a bachelor's degree in elementary education from the University of Missouri-St. Louis in 2004, a graduate degree from Drury University in 2018 and an Ed.S. from Missouri State University in 2023.
Her survey also lists an A.A. in business administration and degrees in elementary, gifted and special education and assessment, and she has worked as an educator.
Hesketh served the city of Forsyth as alderwoman and later as mayor, focusing on recreation and ecotourism, communications and transparency, and enforcement against nuisance and dangerous buildings.
She was the Democratic nominee for this seat in 2024, losing to Burlison 71.6% to 26.3%, and won the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary unopposed.
She describes herself as a single parent of three.
During the campaign, she emphasized ending division and restoring accountability and "decency and decorum" to Congress.
Hesketh received 35.4% of the vote to Eric Burlison's 62.2%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
